regions.name: Deep South Bible Belt
regions.note: the Baptist and Methodist school tradition of the lower South, from Arkansas across to South Carolina

regions.name: Greater South
regions.note: the southern states outside the Deep South core, in three separated groups: the Appalachian states, Texas with Oklahoma, and Florida, which borders none of the others

regions.name: Reformed Heartland and Great Lakes
regions.note: the Dutch Reformed and Lutheran school traditions, which built a dense network of small parochial schools

regions.name: Plains
regions.note: thin populations spread across large distances, where a single school often serves several counties

regions.name: Northeast and Mid-Atlantic
regions.note: nineteenth-century Catholic parochial systems, concentrated in its cities

regions.name: New England Upper
regions.note: three states, thinly settled, with a correspondingly thin Christian school network

regions.name: Mountain West
regions.note: wide distances, small towns, and the widest internal spread of any region

regions.name: Pacific and Frontier
regions.note: geographically the widest, from Hawaii to Alaska, with little in common but the coast

attention_note: Attention is measured for the fifty states. It is not measured for a Christian Education Market Area, so on the attention layer every market area carries the reading of the state it sits in, and the District of Columbia carries none.
provision_note: The school census is the federal private school census. A census is taken, not sampled monthly, so the provision layer steps when a new census lands rather than moving from window to window.
